correctness.rationale: Each diagonal mode has a rank-one two-state error matrix with determinant zero and trace zeta = 1 - alpha*rho*(a+b)/((rho+a)*(rho+b)). Cayley--Hamilton gives M^2=zeta*M, so finite termination for every initial state is equivalent to zeta=0 in every mode. Solving those equalities yields the common-line condition and standard-relaxation slope restriction. The exact rational witness is replayed by the embedded verifier.

value.rationale: Finite termination is a natural extreme of parameter tuning. The theorem gives a complete iff classification for when one scalar penalty and one standard relaxation can annihilate every mode of a heterogeneous separable quadratic consensus problem, separating that possibility from matrix-metric normalization. The line geometry is directly checkable and the two-mode witness shows the phenomenon is not confined to an isotropic block.
